config_name: IdeaPad Slim 3 15.6" — Athlon Silver 10, 8GB LPDDR5, 128GB SSD, FHD

specs.display_type: LCD LED backlight anti-glare (panel type unstated — likely TN)

battery.notes: ~32Wh (4156 mAh) but a 2-core SoC sips power; ~5.5-6.5h light web use despite the small pack.

offers.name: Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3 15.6" Laptop, Business Student - AMD Athlon Silver 10 - 8GB LPDDR5 - 128GB SSD - Windows 11 Home - Abyss Blue

praises: Battery lasts longer than its tiny 32Wh pack suggests because the 2-core chip draws so little
Fine as a dedicated email/documents/Zoom machine for a kid or grandparent
Wi-Fi 6 and USB-C present — connectivity is not ancient like sub-$500 machines
Silent most of the time; fan only whispers under any real load
Light 15.6" chassis at 1.62 kg for a big-screen cheap laptop
complaints: 2-core Athlon makes Windows 11 feel laboured: app launches, Windows Update, and multi-tab browsing all stutter
128GB SSD is nearly full after Windows + OneDrive + Office; buyers upgrade the drive on day one
Panel is the dullest in the family — dim, washed, almost certainly TN
8GB soldered LPDDR5 with no upgrade path on a machine people keep 4+ years
Noticeably slower than the $500-sale Core 5 320 SKU despite costing $700 — wrong trade of money

standouts: Genuinely long battery for the class (~6h) from only 32Wh, thanks to the low-power 2-core SoC
dealbreakers: 2 cores + 128GB in 2026: this is the slowest config in the dataset and the storage is effectively pre-filled
Poor buy at $699.99 when the Core 5 320 SKU sells for $499-599
design_philosophy: The absolute floor of Lenovo's branded budget range: a 2-core Mendocino-class Athlon, 8GB soldered, and a 128GB drive in the 15.6" Slim 3 shell, priced for the 'cheapest name-brand laptop on the shelf' job. Lenovo spends the saved money on nothing visible — this config exists to occupy the entry price point.
rating_notes: No pro review exists for this SKU (Athlon budget tier is ignored by outlets; see SHARED-ideapad-slim3.md). Inferred from Core 5 320 sibling: −2.0 productivity (2-core vs 6-core), −0.5 battery credit for the ultra-low-draw SoC despite 32Wh, screen_quality −1.0 for likely-TN unstated panel, gaming −0.5 (610M is barely usable). Brightness and panel type are class estimates.
